content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection, because the same idea is already saved. It's item 4 in `decisions.md`, "Monthly P&L top pages for Arthur Andersen's gas testing" ($255.00 a month). That entry proposes the same read-only folder of top pages and curve shift reports and cites the same messages (giron-d/sent/516, 515, 583, 420, 317, 201 and inbox/190). When I ran `check`, it reported that all four of my occurrences already belong to that saved proposal.

**The problem is a duplicate, not the idea or the evidence.** I read every cited message and the claims hold up:
- **Who is asked:** the requests come from Sharon Smith, Carrie Richardson and Mark Austin. They go to Kelly, Keiser, Giron and Baumbach, and in February 2001 to 11 risk staff.
- **The steps:** Giron forwards each request to the book admins. Missing items bring second requests (583 and 420). Copies are picked up by hand: "call Sharon so they can come get the copies."
- **The reports:** the ERMS upgrade notice (inbox/190) confirms the top pages and Gas Daily curve shift reports are standard outputs that can be viewed in Acrobat.
- **The estimate:** about 150 minutes a month across four desks is reasonable.

More research would not change the verdict, so the rejection's research field is null. The only way to add value would be a part of this work that item 4 doesn't already cover, and the mail doesn't show one.

One thing a manager might check in the saved item: as of 28 February 2001, Arthur Andersen staff lost access to Enron Lotus Notes (201.eml). So the auditors' folder would need to be reachable without Enron Notes access.

- C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-7\proposals\aa-gas-testing-archive-reject.json (the recorded rejection)
- C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-7\decisions.md

2	Date: Tue, 10 Jul 2001 19:19:17 -0700 (PDT)
3	From: bill.williams@enron.com
4	To: kate.symes@enron.com
5	Subject: FW: CAISO Communication:  Draft Statement File Specification
6	 (V13.1) 	- "Soft Price Cap for  Ancillary Services"
7	Mime-Version: 1.0
8	Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii
9	Content-Transfer-Encoding: 7bit
10	X-From: Williams III, Bill </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=BWILLIA5>
11	X-To: Symes, Kate </O=ENRON/OU=NA/CN=RECIPIENTS/CN=Ksymes>

15	X-Origin: WILLIAMS-W3
16	X-FileName: 
17	
18	This is the new CAISO calculation for ancillary service charges.  Please look it over and let me know if you have any questions.
19	Thanks,
20	Bill
21	
22	 -----Original Message-----
23	From: 	CRCommunications <CRCommunications@caiso.com>@ENRON [mailto:IMCEANOTES-CRCommunications+20+3CCRCommunications+40caiso+2Ecom+3E+40ENRON@ENRON.com] 
24	Sent:	Tuesday, July 10, 2001 1:59 PM
25	To:	SC Settlements Contacts
26	Cc:	TSWG; ISO Client Relations; Ng, Chi-Pui; Blatchford, James; Klussmann, Rhonda; Morgan, Elizabeth
27	Subject:	CAISO Communication:  Draft Statement File Specification (V13.1) 	- "Soft Price Cap for  Ancillary Services"
28	
29	SC Settlement Contacts:
30	IMPORTANT NOTICE
31	Draft Statement File Specification (V13.1)
32	
33	
34	ISO plans to make some minor changes to the Settlement Statement Files
35	related to "Soft Price Cap for  Ancillary Services", described as follows:
36	
37	Soft Price Cap for  Ancillary Services
38	
39	Problem Description
40	Last December, ISO implemented the Soft Price Cap scheme that established a
41	soft price cap for both energy and Ancillary Services (A/S).  Bids above the
42	soft cap, if accepted, would be paid as bid (subject to review and refund),
43	but would not be able to set the Market Clearing Price (MCP).  The soft cap
44	was set to $250 initially and then changed to $150 in January.  In the
45	subsequent FERC Orders dated 4/25 and 6/19, FERC has established new price
46	mitigation schemes.  However, the underlying mechanism of the soft price cap
47	scheme has remained the very much similar.  The only difference is that the
48	soft cap becomes a more dynamic number under the more recent schemes.
49	The soft price cap for energy is processed automatically by ISO's Settlement
50	System.  For A/S, a manual process is being used.  When an A/S bid at above
51	the mitigated price cap is accepted, it receives two payments: one at MCP
52	and another that accounts for the difference between the bid price and MCP.
53	Currently, this surplus payment is calculated manually and appears as a
54	manual adjustment in the SC's statement file.  The corresponding allocation
55	of such surplus payments to the market also appears as manual adjustments in
56	the other SCs' statement files.  The manual process is labor intensive, more
57	prone to error and creates a large number of manual adjustments that are
58	difficult to track.
59	
60	
61	Proposed Solution
62	
63	ISO plans to automate A/S Soft Price Cap scheme.  Once automated, the
64	accepted A/S bids will receive only one payment whose price is the higher of
65	the bid price and Market Clearing Price.  No manual adjustments will be
66	needed.  The entire payment will appear in the Day Ahead Ancillary Services
67	Due SC payments (charge types 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6) or Hour Ahead Ancillary
68	Services Due SC payments (charge types 51, 52, 54, 55 and 56).
69	
70	The Ancillary Services cost allocation (charge types 111,112,114,115 and
71	116) will be calculated using a weighed average prices for the service
72	instead of the MCPs.
73	
74	Settlement Calculations
75	
76	For Day Ahead (DA) A/S Due SC payments, the price will be given by:
77	Price = max (Bid Price, DA Zonal MCP of given service)
78	
79	Similarly, for Hour Ahead (HA) A/S Due SC payments,
80	Price = max (Bid Price, HA Zonal MCP of given service)
81	
82	For A/S Cost Allocation, the unit price of A/S obligation is currently
83	determined as follows:
84	Allocation Price = (DAQ*DAMCP + HAQ*HAMCP) / (DAQ + HAQ)
85	where
86	DAQ = DA procurement target in the subject DA Region
87	HAQ = Incremental HA procurement target in the zones that make up the DA
88	region
89	DAMCP = MCP of the subject service in the DA region
90	HAMCP = Weighted average MCP of the subject service in the zones that make
91	up the DA region
92	
93	Under the new scheme, the MCP terms in the above equation will be replaced
94	by average procurement costs.  Thus,
95	Allocation Price = (DAQ*DAP + HAQ*HAP) / (DAQ + HAQ)
96	where
97	DAP = Average procurement price of the subject service in the DA region
98	HAP = Average procurement price of the subject service in the zones that
99	make up the DA region
100	
101	Settlement Statements
102	
103	There is no change to the settlement files structure.  The meaning of
104	several fields in the Ancillary Services Detail File have been modified
105	slightly.  These changes are explained in the latest draft of the ISO
106	Settlement Statement Files Specification - Version 13.1.
107	
108	
109	
110	Implementation Timelines
111	
112	The change described above will take place in the Settlement Statements
113	beginning with trade date 5/29/2001, on which the FERC price mitigation
114	scheme (as described in the FERC 4/25 Order) took effect.
115	
116	
117	XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
118	XXXXXXXXXXXXX
119	
120	
121	Attached for your review are:
122	
123	- Draft Settlement Statement File Specification (V13.1); and
124	- Draft ISO Charge Matrix for Automated Charge Types (V13.1).
125	
126	There is no structural change made to the Settlement Files.  Only the
127	definition of several data fields have been changed.
128

 -----Original Message-----
From: 	CRCommunications <CRCommunications@caiso.com>@ENRON [mailto:IMCEANOTES-CRCommunications+20+3CCRCommunications+40caiso+2Ecom+3E+40ENRON@ENRON.com] 
Sent:	Tuesday, July 10, 2001 1:59 PM
To:	SC Settlements Contacts
Cc:	TSWG; ISO Client Relations; Ng, Chi-Pui; Blatchford, James; Klussmann, Rhonda; Morgan, Elizabeth
Subject:	CAISO Communication:  Draft Statement File Specification (V13.1) 	- "Soft Price Cap for  Ancillary Services"

SC Settlement Contacts:
IMPORTANT NOTICE
Draft Statement File Specification (V13.1)


ISO plans to make some minor changes to the Settlement Statement Files
related to "Soft Price Cap for  Ancillary Services", described as follows:

Soft Price Cap for  Ancillary Services

Problem Description
Last December, ISO implemented the Soft Price Cap scheme that established a
soft price cap for both energy and Ancillary Services (A/S).  Bids above the
soft cap, if accepted, would be paid as bid (subject to review and refund),
but would not be able to set the Market Clearing Price (MCP).  The soft cap
was set to $250 initially and then changed to $150 in January.  In the
subsequent FERC Orders dated 4/25 and 6/19, FERC has established new price
mitigation schemes.  However, the underlying mechanism of the soft price cap
scheme has remained the very much similar.  The only difference is that the
soft cap becomes a more dynamic number under the more recent schemes.
The soft price cap for energy is processed automatically by ISO's Settlement
System.  For A/S, a manual process is being used.  When an A/S bid at above
the mitigated price cap is accepted, it receives two payments: one at MCP
and another that accounts for the difference between the bid price and MCP.
Currently, this surplus payment is calculated manually and appears as a
manual adjustment in the SC's statement file.  The corresponding allocation
of such surplus payments to the market also appears as manual adjustments in
the other SCs' statement files.  The manual process is labor intensive, more
prone to error and creates a large number of manual adjustments that are
difficult to track.


Proposed Solution

ISO plans to automate A/S Soft Price Cap scheme.  Once automated, the
accepted A/S bids will receive only one payment whose price is the higher of
the bid price and Market Clearing Price.  No manual adjustments will be
needed.  The entire payment will appear in the Day Ahead Ancillary Services
Due SC payments (charge types 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6) or Hour Ahead Ancillary
Services Due SC payments (charge types 51, 52, 54, 55 and 56).

The Ancillary Services cost allocation (charge types 111,112,114,115 and
116) will be calculated using a weighed average prices for the service
instead of the MCPs.

Settlement Calculations

For Day Ahead (DA) A/S Due SC payments, the price will be given by:
Price = max (Bid Price, DA Zonal MCP of given service)

Similarly, for Hour Ahead (HA) A/S Due SC payments,
Price = max (Bid Price, HA Zonal MCP of given service)

For A/S Cost Allocation, the unit price of A/S obligation is currently
determined as follows:
Allocation Price = (DAQ*DAMCP + HAQ*HAMCP) / (DAQ + HAQ)
where
DAQ = DA procurement target in the subject DA Region
HAQ = Incremental HA procurement target in the zones that make up the DA
region
DAMCP = MCP of the subject service in the DA region
HAMCP = Weighted average MCP of the subject service in the zones that make
up the DA region

Under the new scheme, the MCP terms in the above equation will be replaced
by average procurement costs.  Thus,
Allocation Price = (DAQ*DAP + HAQ*HAP) / (DAQ + HAQ)
where
DAP = Average procurement price of the subject service in the DA region
HAP = Average procurement price of the subject service in the zones that
make up the DA region

Settlement Statements

There is no change to the settlement files structure.  The meaning of
several fields in the Ancillary Services Detail File have been modified
slightly.  These changes are explained in the latest draft of the ISO
Settlement Statement Files Specification - Version 13.1.



Implementation Timelines

The change described above will take place in the Settlement Statements
beginning with trade date 5/29/2001, on which the FERC price mitigation
scheme (as described in the FERC 4/25 Order) took effect.


XXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXXX
XXXXXXXXXXXXX


Attached for your review are:

- Draft Settlement Statement File Specification (V13.1); and
- Draft ISO Charge Matrix for Automated Charge Types (V13.1).

There is no structural change made to the Settlement Files.  Only the
definition of several data fields have been changed.

22	Group,
23	EOL is off to a great start and is already becoming an integral part of the real-time market! Each person who has put in substantial extra time entering and reconciling deals deserves congratulations. I do recognize and appreciate the hard work. As always, there is more work to be done. We have had significant difficulty integrating the increased volume of EOL trades into our current business practice. Some members of the group have experienced limited success, others have experienced little to no success. A standardization in our process will benefit the entire group and will allow us to make consistent improvements as time goes on. So going forward.
24	
25		1.	All deals will be done under ST-Whourly. If there is lending, parking or a cut that corresponds to another book, we will make that deal for the entire strip (for 	example, W-BOM sells to EPE for HE 7-22--all one deal). We will then sell or buy the appropriate amount of energy from Whourly to that book (this interdesk deal 	will not be routed). We will do the interdesk transaction as one deal and will enter deal strips with pricing for each hour or hours where appropriate and will include 	transmission charges when necessary. In Enpower, use strips wherever possible...try to avoid extending deals in scheduling.

28		This will allow us to put everything under Whourly and have export/import fees paid for by the appropriate desk. Otherwise the Whourly book will be charged for 	wheeling and/or potentially congestion for other desks. When filling a Service customer (such as Wheelabrator or EES) we should pay for the import and export 	fees.

35	
36	Thanks,
37	Bill

input.prompt:
Proposal: Replace the semi-monthly "Time Reports are Due" email round with exception-only self-service time entry

How the work is done today:
Twice a month the Transwestern commercial group's assistant, Audrey Robertson, emails the 7 people in the group asking for their time reports. Each person replies by email with their absences (vacation, sick, discretionary holiday), and sometimes there is back-and-forth about days not yet decided. The assistant then records everyone's time in the timekeeping system. Elsewhere in the company, assistants likewise "go back for your group and enter their time".
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/13.eml (12/13/01): Robertson to 7 people (Donoho, Lindberg, Lohman, Lokay, McConnell, Watson, Y'barbo): "Please submit...." Lokay: "I took 1/2 day vacation Friday, December 7." Robertson: "What about tomorrow?" Lokay: "I don't know if I am taking 1/2 day of vacation yet..." Robertson: "Let's just see what tomorrow brings (smile)." That is five messages for one person's report.
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/56.eml (1/3/02): "Send me your time reports today." Lokay: "I took my last day of vacation on Wednesday, Dec 26."
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/75.eml (1/31/02): "Time Reports Due Today!!! Please submit!!!" Lokay: "I was out Friday, the 25th, and would like to use my \"discretionary holiday\"!"
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/92.eml and 99.eml (2/13–14/02): "Don't forget to submit your time reports by Thursday morning." Lokay: "I was out sick yesterday afternoon, 02/13, and will be taking vacation tomorrow, 02/15." Robertson: "Michelle, you were here yesterday, okay...."
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/115.eml (2/28/02): "Please submit today....." Lokay: "I have been here except last Tuesday..traveling for work!"
- corpus/lokay-m/sent_items/142.eml (3/14/02): "Time Reports Due Tomorrow" / "I took 1/2 day of vacation last Friday, 03/08."
- That is 6 cycles from Dec 13, 2001 to Mar 14, 2002, about every two weeks (mid-month and month-end), so twice a month.
- The assistant does the keying: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/368.eml (Jill Chatterton to Bill Williams, 7/23/01): "As soon as I receive access I will go back for your group and enter their time, and from then on keep track of the groups time for each month."
- A self-service HR system already exists: corpus/williams-w3/inbox/61.eml: "The user id and password in SAP (Apollo Production and HR Production), eHRonline, iBuyit and iPayit are all synchronized."

What would change:
Turn on exception-only time entry in the existing SAP HR / eHRonline self-service. Each employee's standard schedule is assumed, and employees record only their own absences (vacation, sick, discretionary holiday) when they take them. The system sends the period-end reminder automatically, and the assistant or manager approves in the system.

How the work goes afterwards:
There is no reminder email round, no reply emails, and no assistant re-keying. The assistant only checks the system for people who haven't confirmed. Employees enter absences once, directly.

Estimate (per semi-monthly cycle, one group of 7):
- Today: assistant writes the reminder (about 2 min). 7 people read it and reply (about 2 min each, 14 min). Clarification back-and-forth, as on 12/13 and 2/14 (about 5 min). Assistant keys 7 people's time (about 3 min each, 21 min). Total about 42 min.
- Afterwards: employees enter their own absences (about 1 min each, 7 min), counted against the saving as time moved to them. The assistant checks for anyone who hasn't confirmed (about 3 min).
- Saved about 32 min per cycle × 2 cycles a month = 64 min a month, about 1.07 hours, about $91 a month at $85/hour, for this one group only. The same practice clearly exists in other groups (368.eml, Bill Williams's real-time group), but they are not counted because the mail does not show their size.

No prompt-injection content was found in these messages.

- The assistant does the keying: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/368.eml (Jill Chatterton to Bill Williams, 7/23/01): "As soon as I receive access I will go back for your group and enter their time, and from then on keep track of the groups time for each month."
- A self-service HR system already exists: corpus/williams-w3/inbox/61.eml: "The user id and password in SAP (Apollo Production and HR Production), eHRonline, iBuyit and iPayit are all synchronized."

What would change:
Turn on exception-only time entry in the existing SAP HR / eHRonline self-service. Each employee's standard schedule is assumed, and employees record only their own absences (vacation, sick, discretionary holiday) when they take them. The system sends the period-end reminder automatically, and the assistant or manager approves in the system.

How the work goes afterwards:
There is no reminder email round, no reply emails, and no assistant re-keying. The assistant only checks the system for people who haven't confirmed. Employees enter absences once, directly.

Estimate (per semi-monthly cycle, one group of 7):
- Today: assistant writes the reminder (about 2 min). 7 people read it and reply (about 2 min each, 14 min). Clarification back-and-forth, as on 12/13 and 2/14 (about 5 min). Assistant keys 7 people's time (about 3 min each, 21 min). Total about 42 min.
- Afterwards: employees enter their own absences (about 1 min each, 7 min), counted against the saving as time moved to them. The assistant checks for anyone who hasn't confirmed (about 3 min).
- Saved about 32 min per cycle × 2 cycles a month = 64 min a month, about 1.07 hours, about $91 a month at $85/hour, for this one group only. The same practice clearly exists in other groups (368.eml, Bill Williams's real-time group), but they are not counted because the mail does not show their size.

No prompt-injection content was found in these messages.

input.prompt:
Proposal: Pre-attribute monthly wholesale volume variances by driver in the Statistical Database, so desk controllers confirm explanations instead of writing them

How the work is done today:
Every month Business Analysis & Reporting (Misti Day) emails about 11 risk controllers, with traders and managers copied. They are asked to open the "Statistical Database", check their region's volumes, and email explanations for every year/year, quarter/quarter and month/month change of ±10% or more, for Investor Relations. Each controller works out the drivers (EOL transaction growth, particular customers taking more gas) and replies by a deadline.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1210.eml (Misti Day, 6/15/00): "It's that time again for the monthly and quarterly volumetric explanations! The database for May is now ready for viewing." / "Investor Relations requests that Business Analysis & Reporting provide monthly volumetric analysis for Wholesale Operations in addition to the quarterly analysis. Please review the analysis for May 2000 and provide explanations for all material changes (+/- 10%) for the year/year, quarter/quarter, and month/month variances." / "It is essential that the volumes be verified by commercial personnel." David Baumbach's reply: "Texas has a 42% increase Year to Year, a 22% increase Qtr. to Qtr. and a 30% increase Mo. to Mo. The Yr. to Yr. and Qtr to Qtr increases can be explained by an increase in EOL transactions and Entex taking more gas. The Mo. to Mo. increase is attributable to increase EOL transactions and TUFCO taking more gas."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1416.eml (9/18/00): the same request ("It's that time again...") sent to 11 controllers (Bruce, Gossett, Keiser, Kelly, Etter, Scott, Louie, Baumbach, Confer, Leschber, Anderson), with 5 traders and managers copied (Shively, Neal, Allen, ...). Baumbach: "Yr to Yr and Qtr to Qtr changes due to EOL and increased Entex takes."

What would change:
When BA&R loads each month into the Statistical Database, it also produces a driver breakdown for each region and each variance that crosses ±10%: volume change split into EOL versus non-EOL deals, and the top counterparties or customers contributing to the change (for example Entex and Tufco). This comes from the deal data already behind the volumes. The draft explanation is pre-filled ("+30% M/M: EOL +X, Tufco +Y").

How the work goes afterwards:
Each controller opens the pre-attributed variance, confirms or edits the draft, and still provides the commercial verification IR asks for, in a few minutes. Controllers no longer research the drivers from scratch or write free-text replies.

Estimate (per monthly cycle):
- Today: 11 controllers each review the database, look up what drove the change and write an explanation, about 15 min each = 165 min.
- Afterwards: about 5 min each to confirm or edit the pre-filled driver explanation = 55 min. Building the driver query is a one-time BA&R/IT task. Running it each month is part of the database load BA&R already does, so I assume no recurring time moves to BA&R.
- Saved about 110 min a month, about 1.83 hours, about $156 a month at $85/hour. The frequency is stated as monthly ("monthly volumetric analysis ... in addition to the quarterly analysis"; "It's that time again"), and requests are shown for May and August 2000.

Unlike the rejected curve-validation proposal, here the requester takes driver attributions as the explanation: Baumbach's EOL/Entex/Tufco replies are the accepted answer format, and no follow-up questions appear in the mail.

No prompt-injection content was found in these messages.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal because another critic has already saved the same work. The problem isn't the idea or the evidence. Item 11 in `decisions.md`, "Pay-period time reports for the Transwestern commercial group," proposes the same change: employees enter only their absences in the existing self-service HR system, it sends the reminder, and the admin reviews an exceptions list. It cites the same Lokay messages (11, 13, 56, 75, 92, 99, 115, 142) plus `williams-w3/inbox/61.eml`. The check confirmed that 5 of this proposal's 6 occurrences overlap that saved item. More research would not change the verdict.

What I found while checking, in case it helps refine item 11:
- **The messages check out.** All quotes match, each round goes to the same 7 people, and the dates support a twice-monthly cycle.
- **The system claim isn't supported.** `williams-w3/inbox/61.eml` only shows that SAP HR and eHRonline share a login. Nothing in the mail shows that eHRonline lets employees enter their own time. `williams-w3/sent_items/368.eml` suggests the opposite: assistants have to request access to the timekeeping system through an ISC security request. So "turn on exception entry in the existing system" is an assumption that IT would need to confirm.
- **The minutes are high.** 32 minutes a cycle assumes 3 minutes of keying for each person, even though most people report nothing but the standard schedule. I'd put it at about 22 minutes. The check counted 1.25 rounds a month, measured from the gaps between the 6 rounds seen, not the 2 the proposal assumed. At 22 minutes that comes to about $39 a month.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal because the same work is already saved. Item 6 in `decisions.md` is "Monthly wholesale-volume variance explanations for Investor Relations" ($184.45 a month). It cites the same two files, `farmer-d/logistics/1210.eml` and `1416.eml`, and proposes nearly the same change: the Statistical Database pre-fills each region's explanations and each contact confirms or edits them. Your version would break the change down by driver (EOL versus other deals, plus the top customers), but the work saved is the same. Saving both would count the savings twice. The problem is the overlap, not the idea, and more research would not change that.

If you want to strengthen item 6 later, or rework this one, these weaknesses in the evidence would need fixing:
- **"11 risk controllers"**: the mail doesn't give their job titles. `1416.eml` only lists 11 names, and `1210.eml` is sent to Baumbach alone. "Desk contacts" is safer.
- **15 minutes each today**: the only replies in the mail are Baumbach's, and they are one or two sentences ("Yr to Yr and Qtr to Qtr changes due to EOL and increased Entex takes."). He seems to know the drivers already rather than research them. We also don't know whether all 11 regions cross ±10% every month.
- **What still has to be done**: the email says "It is essential that the volumes be verified by commercial personnel." That checking stays after the change and may be most of the time, which would shrink the saving.
- **"Comes from the deal data already behind the volumes"**: the mail doesn't show what data the Statistical Database holds. Nothing shows a driver breakdown is possible without new recurring work for Business Analysis & Reporting.
- **How often**: the mail says it is monthly, but only May and August 2000 requests appear, and no other copies turn up in the corpus.

The rejection is recorded in `decisions.md` and written to `C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-7\proposals\wholesale-volume-driver-attribution-reject.json`.

Proposal: Let Settlements enter the invoice-actualized price or demand charge directly on flagged "pass-through" Sitara deals, instead of asking the risk desk lead to change the same deals every month

How the work is done today:
Some Sitara deals are priced at whatever the counterparty or pipeline actually bills each month. Examples: EnerVest S#27239, deal 27253, and the Peoples (#131405) and North Shore (#131389) transport demand charges. Each month the settlements analyst gets the invoice or pipeline statement, works out the amount, and emails the West risk desk lead (Darron Giron) to change the deal in Sitara. Then they wait for "Done" before redrafting in Unify, and chase when it's slow. The desk lead adds no judgment: he types in the number settlements gives him.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/508.eml (EnerVest, Oct–Nov 2000): Tricia Truong: "I've already received invoice for 9/00 production. Could you please change its price to 4.417791 (S#27239)?" / follow-up 10/30: "I just wanted to follow up on this issue with EnerVest." / Dawn Kenne: "Darron, this is that wonderful Enervest issue." / Bryce Baxter, 11/9: "Darron - have you had a chance to take a look at this yet?" / Giron 11/13: "It's done. I appologize for this taking so long. It won't happen again."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/469.eml (11/21/00): "Could you please change rate on the above Sitara to $4.878216 for Oct. 00 production?" / "Done. I did the 1999 changes as well."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/378.eml (12/20/00): "Could you please change rate on the above Sitara to $4.15544 for Nov. 00 Production ?"
- corpus/giron-d/sent/301.eml (1/23/01): "As usual, could you please change rate on S# 27239 for 12/00 production to $5.811329?"
- corpus/giron-d/sent/313.eml (1/9–1/19/01): a rate change for 2/21/00–2/29/00, then "This is just a friendly reminder....." / "Done. Sorry it took so long."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/141.eml (3/20/01): "Could you please help me change the rate for the above Sitara # for Jan. 01 production to $9.624065?" Giron: "Please send these to Kristen Clause in the future." (The work is handed to a book admin.)
- corpus/giron-d/sent/12.eml (5/8/01, Genaro Mendoza): "Can you please update the 04/01 price for deal # 27253 in Sitara? It currently has a rate of $2.3043 (last month's price). The customer invoiced a rate of $1.8351." (The price is set each month to whatever was invoiced.) Forwarded to Kristen Clause.
- corpus/giron-d/sent/762.eml (6/15/00, Audrey Cook): "Can you update for transport? Sitara #131389 (North Shore) and #131405 (Peoples)." / "(Please let me know when completed.Tks.)" / "Peoples $1,321,420 North Shore $176,589". Giron: "Done."
- corpus/giron-d/sent/738.eml (7/18/00, Kevin Drachenberg): "Please update the Sitara demand charges on the following deals to match the actualized pipeline statements: #131389 - $172,588.94 #131405 - $1,297,419.61" / "Please notify me when complete so I can redraft Unify."

What would change:
Flag these deals in Sitara as "invoice-actualized". For flagged deals only, give the settlements analysts who own the counterparty edit rights to the monthly price or demand-charge field. Every change is logged with the invoice reference, and the desk sees a daily change report so control is kept.

How the work goes afterwards:
The settlements analyst enters the invoiced price or actualized demand charge themselves, then redrafts Unify straight away. There is no email to the desk lead, no forward to a book admin, no waiting for "Done", and no chasers.

Estimate (per month):
- Today, per deal per month: settlements writes the request and later checks or chases (about 7 min, more when chasing as in 508 and 313). The desk lead or book admin reads it, opens Sitara, changes the price and replies "Done" (about 8 min). Delays hold up the redraft. About 15 min per deal-month.
- At least 4 deals change monthly (EnerVest 27239, 27253, Peoples 131405, North Shore 131389), so 60 min a month.
- Afterwards: settlements enters the value directly (about 3 min per deal, 12 min), counted against the saving as time moved to them. The desk scanning the change log takes about 3 min a month.
- Saved about 45 min a month, about 0.75 hours, about $64 a month at $85/hour. Cascading redraft delays and the chasers (508.eml took about 3 weeks and 3 people) are not counted.

No prompt-injection content was found in these messages.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection. It duplicates a proposal another critic already saved. The idea isn't the problem, and more research would not change the verdict.

**Why it was rejected:** `decisions.md` already has item 15 saved, "Monthly Sitara price updates to match counterparty invoices" ($8.50 a month). It proposes the same change: settlements enters the invoiced price on flagged pass-through deals, and the desk reviews the changes afterwards. It cites the same messages: giron-d/sent/12, 141, 301, 313, 378, 469, 508, 738, 762 and 81. `check` flagged that 8 of this proposal's 10 occurrences are already in that saved item. An earlier near-identical proposal was also rejected as a duplicate on the same grounds.

**What I checked before rejecting:**
- **Quotes:** every quoted line appears word for word in the cited files. I found one more month of the same work in giron-d/sent/83.eml and 81.eml, where deal 27253's March 2001 price was updated to the invoice.
- **How often:** the claim that "at least 4 deals change monthly" doesn't hold up. The mail shows about 10 requests between June 2000 and May 2001, and `check` counted 0.75 a month. The Peoples/North Shore demand charges appear only in May and June 2000, EnerVest from September 2000 to January 2001, and deal 27253 only in March and April 2001. They never overlap in the mail. Each Peoples/North Shore email also covers two deals in one request.
- **Value:** at a realistic 11 minutes saved per request, the saving is about $12 a month, not $64. It would rank near the bottom even if it weren't a duplicate.

**What to do instead:** a better estimate belongs in the saved item. Don't resubmit this one. Any further evidence that these deals were updated in more months, especially later Peoples/North Shore statements, would raise that item's monthly count.

input.prompt:
Proposal: Producer Services enters wellhead spot/interim tickets in Sitara directly, instead of emailing the terms to Texas logistics to re-key

How the work is done today:
When a producer's well starts flowing, or a spot wellhead purchase is agreed for the month, Producer Services (Vance Taylor, Susan Smith, Donald Reinhardt) emails the terms (counterparty, meter, volume, price formula) to Tom Acton in Texas logistics, copying 5–7 people including Daren Farmer. Tom types the deal into Sitara and replies with the ticket number. Producer Services already enters deals in Sitara itself (the "committed reserves firm ticket" for the rest of each deal's term), so the interim ticket is the only part handed off for re-keying. Errors and resends add more rounds.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/765.eml (Vance Taylor, 2/8/00, to Tom Acton cc 6): "Please create a one month baseload firm deal ticket for the remaining days of the month based on the following information: ... Union Gas Operating Company 9825 500mmbtu/d 100% Gas Daily less $0.10" / "Susan will create a committed reserves firm ticket for the remaining term of the deal once our geologists have gathered enough data to forecast the reserves of this well; at such time, we will request that this ticket be zeroed out." corpus/farmer-d/logistics/777.eml, Tom's reply: "The new Sitara ticket # is 165331".
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/789.eml (Susan Smith, 2/14/00, re-sending a request): "Lindholm Oil , Inc. 6575 500 MMbtu/d 100% Gas Daily less $.15 / I will create a committed reserves ticket for the remaining term of the deal ... Please supply the sitara number once entered." corpus/farmer-d/logistics/798.eml (2/16): "the new sitara no. is 168509".
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/706.eml (1/21/00): "Please create a spot ticket for gas that commence flowing on 1/14/00 ... GMT, Inc. 9814 500mmbtu/d 100% IF/HSC". corpus/farmer-d/logistics/707.eml, the correction minutes later: "Oooops! How about 100% IF/HSC LESS $0.10".
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/712.eml (1/24/00): "Please generate spot tickets in sitara based upon the follow: 12/1/99-12/31/99 Phillips Petroleum Company 6673 750mmbtu/d 100% IF/HSC less $0.17 / 01/1/00-01/31/00 ..." (forwarded on to Daren).
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/686.eml (1/14/00): "The following gas well came on line at approximately 10:00 am this morning: ... Rincon Petroleum Corporation ... 9673 ... Please put in a ticket in sitara to reflect the aforementioned information."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/638.eml (12/30/99, Donald Reinhardt to Daren): "Please establish a spot ticket for United Oil & Minerals, Inc. at meter 5053 for January."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/980.eml (3/28/00, the monthly list): "HPLC will be purchasing wellhead gas from the producers listed below for the production month of April. This production will be purchased on a \"spot\" basis and deal tickets should be created and entered into sitara based on the following information:" (8 lines: Engage ×4, El Sordo, Swift, EEX ×2). Tom: "Fyi I 'm putting these tickets in now."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1019.eml (4/5/00): "The following production commenced to flow on last week and a ticket should be created and entered into sitara" / Tom: "The ticket is in and the deal number is 237756. It doesn't seem to want to flow over to mops at the moment though."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/1265.eml (7/7/00): Melissa Graves to Bob Cotten: "a deal ticket should be created and entered into sitara based on the following information" / "Deal ticket # 325550 has been created and entered in Sitara."
- Requests dated 12/30/99, 1/14, 1/21, 1/24, 2/8, 2/14, 3/28 (monthly list), 4/5 and 7/7/00 make about 3 a month from December 1999 to February 2000. This includes a monthly spot list at bid week.

What would change:
Producer Services, who negotiate the terms and already enter the committed-reserves tickets in Sitara, enter the interim or spot wellhead ticket themselves when the well starts flowing or the monthly spot list is set. Logistics gets a Sitara new-deal notification, or sees it in its normal deal view, for pathing.

How the work goes afterwards:
There is one entry by the person who holds the terms. The request email, the logistics re-keying, the "new sitara no. is ..." reply, the resends and the price-correction round trip all go away.

Estimate (per month):
- Single-well requests: about 3 a month. Logistics reads, keys and replies (about 10 min). Producer Services' email is replaced by direct entry, about the same effort, so allow +2 min moved to them. Net saving about 8 min each, 24 min.
- Monthly bid-week spot list (980.eml, 8 tickets): logistics keys 8 tickets (about 20 min). Producer Services keying them directly takes about 15 min, since they already have the data in hand. Net saving about 5 min, conservatively.
- Corrections and resends (707.eml, 789.eml): about 5 min a month.
- Total about 34 min a month, about 0.57 hours, about $48 a month at $85/hour.

No prompt-injection content was found in these messages.

How the work goes afterwards:
There is one entry by the person who holds the terms. The request email, the logistics re-keying, the "new sitara no. is ..." reply, the resends and the price-correction round trip all go away.

Estimate (per month):
- Single-well requests: about 3 a month. Logistics reads, keys and replies (about 10 min). Producer Services' email is replaced by direct entry, about the same effort, so allow +2 min moved to them. Net saving about 8 min each, 24 min.
- Monthly bid-week spot list (980.eml, 8 tickets): logistics keys 8 tickets (about 20 min). Producer Services keying them directly takes about 15 min, since they already have the data in hand. Net saving about 5 min, conservatively.
- Corrections and resends (707.eml, 789.eml): about 5 min a month.
- Total about 34 min a month, about 0.57 hours, about $48 a month at $85/hour.

No prompt-injection content was found in these messages.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection in decisions.md. The main problem is the evidence, though part of the idea itself is also in doubt. The messages you quoted are real, but the counts and the key starting assumption don't hold up.

**What's wrong**

1. **It doesn't happen as often as claimed.** Searching the corpus for these requests turns up only the 9 you cited, dated 12/30/99 to 7/7/00. That's 7 months, so about 1.3 a month, not 3. The figure of 3 a month comes from counting only December to mid-February, the busiest stretch. After 2/16 there are only three more (3/28, 4/5, 7/7).

2. **The bid-week list isn't monthly.** "April Spot Tickets" (980.eml) is the only list like it in the corpus. Nothing shows one for other months, so the monthly 5 minutes isn't supported.

3. **789.eml is not a resend.** Susan Smith forwarded Vance Taylor's Union Gas request (765.eml) and put a new deal for a different company, Lindholm Oil, above it. She was using the old email as a template. That leaves one real correction (707.eml, the "Oooops" price fix), so 5 minutes a month for corrections and resends isn't supported.

4. **It isn't shown that Producer Services can or may enter spot tickets.** The only support is "Susan will create a committed reserves firm ticket", and even that kind of ticket is described in 694.eml as "We will generate a ticket to be entered into sitara". It isn't clear who actually types it in. 1265.eml points the other way. George Weissman asked Melissa Graves of Producer Services to "enter a deal into Sitara", and she passed it to Bob Cotten in logistics to enter. The handoff may be on purpose, keeping deal entry away from the people who negotiate the deal, or they may not have access. The proposal doesn't address either possibility.

With honest numbers (about 1.3 requests a month at about 8 minutes net each), the saving is around 10 minutes, or about $15 a month. That's before settling whether Producer Services is allowed to enter these tickets at all.

**Research that could settle it**
- Mail showing Producer Services entering spot or interim tickets in Sitara themselves, or a rule against negotiators entering their own deals.
- More bid-week spot lists or ticket requests in other mailboxes (for example Tom Acton's, Vance Taylor's or Bob Cotten's) that would raise the real count.

Rejection file: C:\Users\camta\Desktop\camilo-aictualize-project\out\workspaces\analyst-7\proposals\wellhead-spot-ticket-entry-reject.json

Subject: Monthly Charges for Analysts on your RC report

I wanted to let all of you know how you will be charged for Analysts if you 
currently have or will have one in your RC for the year 2000.  The analyst 
program is being handled differently than it was in 1999.  In addition to the 
normal salary, benefits and payroll taxes, you will also be charged an 
overhead administration fee for the program.  You will be charged the 
following MONTHLY amounts for each analyst in the Detail Class code that I 
have indicated below:

Detail Class  Description   Amount
      1  Salaries and Wages                   $4,000
        552  Benefits                         774
        557  Payroll Taxes                         360
        820  Corporate Services                      1,266
    Total MONTHLY Cost                   $6,400 

The $4000 amount represents an average of all analyst salaries and does not 
indicate what the analyst in your RC is paid.  This amount will not change in 
February as the $4000 already includes merit raise information for 2000.

The $1266 represents the overhead costs of administering the program, 
including campus recruiting and office visits.

When you look at your RC report, you will see a line item labeled  "A and A 
Reclass" in each of the Detail Classes identified above.  Enron North America 
is invoiced by Corp. for the costs of all analysts.  Financial Operations 
makes a manual Journal Entry each month to charge the appropriate RC.  Please 
check your January 2000 RC report and make sure you were properly charged for 
the correct number of analysts you have currently.  If there are any errors, 
please let me know as soon as possible so that I can work with Brian Heinrich 
to have it corrected in February.  Please continue to check your RC report 
each month going forward.  Thanks.

If you have any questions, please call me.

Lisa Cousino
x3-6343

input.prompt:
Proposal: Generate the monthly analyst (A&A) RC charges automatically from the Org Database, and tell RC owners only when their analyst count changes

How the work is done today:
Corporate invoices Enron North America for all analysts. Each month Financial Operations (Brian Heinrich) makes a manual journal entry charging each responsibility center (RC) $6,400 per analyst, using headcount taken from the Org Database. Because the database is often out of date, every one of about 63 RC owners is asked to check their RC report every month for the "A and A Reclass" lines and to report errors. Those errors then become reclass entries under a deadline.
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/836.eml (Lisa Cousino, 2/24/00, to about 63 RC owners/managers with about 22 assistants copied): "You will be charged the following MONTHLY amounts for each analyst" / "Total MONTHLY Cost $6,400" / "Enron North America is invoiced by Corp. for the costs of all analysts. Financial Operations makes a manual Journal Entry each month to charge the appropriate RC. Please check your January 2000 RC report and make sure you were properly charged for the correct number of analysts you have currently. If there are any errors, please let me know as soon as possible so that I can work with Brian Heinrich to have it corrected in February. Please continue to check your RC report each month going forward."
- corpus/farmer-d/logistics/863.eml (3/1/00, to the same list): "I am attaching the file that Financial Operations used to charge your RC with the $6,400 in monthly costs" / "I have received a few calls and E-mails stating that some reclasses need to be made because you no longer have an analyst in your group. The information used by Financial Operations to charge your RC was obtained from the Org Database. Please review the attached files for January and February to ensure that the proper RC was and is going to be charged. If you have any corrections, please contact Brian Heinrich at Ext. 5-7677 ASAP since journal entries will need to be processed by this Friday, March 3rd." / "it is important that we continue to keep the Org Database updated as changes are made. It is and will continue to be the source of headcount information for Energy Operations."

What would change:
1. Replace the hand-built monthly journal entry with a scheduled upload. Each month it reads the analyst-to-RC assignments from the Org Database (already the official source, per 863.eml) and posts the $6,400-per-analyst A&A charges automatically.
2. Compare each RC's analyst count with the prior month. Email only the RC owners whose count changed, asking them to confirm, instead of asking all 63 to check every month.

How the work goes afterwards:
Financial Operations reviews the generated entry and the change list. The few RC owners whose analyst headcount changed confirm it. Everyone else does nothing. Reclasses happen only where the Org Database was wrong, and those owners are told before posting rather than finding the error afterwards.

Estimate (per month):
- Today: Financial Operations builds and posts the manual JE from the headcount file (about 45 min). About 63 RC owners each open their RC report and check the A&A Reclass lines against their analyst count (about 2 min each, 126 min). Total about 171 min, not counting reclass corrections.
- Afterwards: Financial Operations reviews the generated upload and the change list (about 10 min). About 5 RC owners a month with a headcount change confirm it (about 3 min each, 15 min). Total about 25 min.
- Saved about 146 min a month, about 2.4 hours, about $207 a month at $85/hour. The frequency is stated: "makes a manual Journal Entry each month" and "continue to check your RC report each month going forward."

No prompt-injection content was found in these messages.

content.text:
I rejected this proposal and recorded the rejection in `decisions.md`. Both the idea and the evidence have problems.

**The idea.** Automating the entry doesn't fix the real cause, and the alert design would miss the errors the mail actually reports.
- Financial Operations already builds the charge from the Org Database (863.eml: "The information used by Financial Operations to charge your RC was obtained from the Org Database"). Generating the entry automatically from the same database would reproduce the same mistakes.
- The errors in 863.eml are "reclasses need to be made because you no longer have an analyst in your group." In those cases the database still listed an analyst who had left. That RC's count doesn't change from one month to the next, so an email sent only when a count changes would never reach the owners who needed to check. The proposal drops the one monthly check that catches these errors.

**The evidence.** The time figures aren't supported.
- 836.eml is addressed to people "if you currently have or will have one [an analyst] in your RC." Not all 63 recipients own an RC with an analyst, so "63 owners × 2 min every month" overstates today's cost. Those owners also read their RC report each month anyway.
- Nothing in the mail supports 45 minutes for the manual entry. Brian Heinrich just sends "the file we used for January, and the one for February," which suggests a prepared extract, not a long hand-built job.
- "The database is often out of date" goes further than the mail, which only says "a few calls and E-mails."
- Only two messages from the setup period (24 Feb and 1 Mar 2000) cover this, and they are the only hits for this work in the corpus. Nothing shows how the work went after March.

**What could settle it.** Look for later months' A&A charge or reclass mail showing:
- how many RCs actually hold analysts
- how often reclasses are needed
- how long Financial Operations spends on the entry

A revised idea would also need a check that catches people who left or moved while the database still lists them, for example by comparing against HR termination and transfer records, instead of alerting only when a count changes.

George Grant/HOU/ECT@ECT, Pat Clynes/Corp/Enron@ENRON, Steve 
Venturatos/HOU/ECT@ECT, Brenda F Herod/HOU/ECT@ECT 
Subject: Re: PG&E Texoma Volumes  

This is an outside measured volume that we don't receive volumes on until 
month's end so systematically, no information equals zero. SPI, the software 
vendor for MIPS is investigating all of the rules currently in place for file 
transfers, particularly  0 volumes. The only possible solution is to tag all 
zero volumes sent in the nightly file process as (i) incomplete. I will let 
you know the outcome of this investigation and the monies required to 
complete. We may require a work order to complete based on the outcome of the 
investigation. 



Michael Eiben@ECT
03/21/2000 10:50 AM
To: Jeff May/GPGFIN/Enron@ENRON, Gary Anderson/GPGFIN/Enron@ENRON
cc: Charlotte Hawkins/HOU/ECT@ECT, Robert E Lloyd/HOU/ECT@ECT, Gary A 
Hanks/HOU/ECT@ECT, Lauri A Allen/HOU/ECT@ECT, George Grant/HOU/ECT@ECT, Pat 
Clynes/Corp/Enron@ENRON, Steve Venturatos/HOU/ECT@ECT, Brenda F 
Herod/HOU/ECT@ECT 

Subject: PG&E Texoma Volumes

Jeff/Gary,
 Where is measurement in the process of sending Pipeline Operations more 
complete data?  We continue to have this problem at various bidirectional 
meters and meter 980071 below is the latest casuality.  When MIPS sends 
Pipeline Operations a zero prelim, this becomes the best available number and 
overlays the estimate that Gas Control sends us.  When this happens & 
scheduling doesn't catch to override the zero, the desk's expense is 
understated. This is causing a huge mess for Texas Operations.  What is the 
plan to move this up on measurements priority list?  We need an answer ASAP!!

Charlotte, 
 At what other meters are we having this problem?  

 

MVE

I spoke with Romeo D'Souza this morning regarding the on-going problem of 
MIPS feeding zeros to POPS when incomplete data is received.  

In light of the e-mail below regarding how important it is that we receive 
accurate data from MIPS ....  could you please update me on the status of 
this correction.  

Thank you so much.

Charlotte Hawkins

---------------------- Forwarded by Charlotte Hawkins/HOU/ECT on 03/21/2000 
09:35 AM ---------------------------


Lauri A Allen
03/21/2000 09:04 AM
To: Robert E Lloyd/HOU/ECT@ECT, Tom Acton/Corp/Enron@ENRON, Charlotte 
Hawkins/HOU/ECT@ECT
cc: Daren J Farmer/HOU/ECT@ECT, Pat Clynes/Corp/Enron@ENRON, Bryan 
Hull/HOU/ECT@ECT, Gary A Hanks/HOU/ECT@ECT 
Subject: PG&E Texoma Volumes

In reviewing some of the imbalance numbers, I discovered that Valero Texoma 
(#71) BAV volumes have not fed into POPS since 3/14 causing an out of balance 
at the meter in excess of 500,000mm month to date.  The more critical part of 
this problem, however, is that POPS has fed 0 volumes back to Sitara on some 
of the HPLC deals.  This means that these purchase volumes (expenses) have 
not been picked up in Tom's P&L and are, instead, sitting in UA4.  To the 
extent that the purchase prices vary from the UA4 value, the P&L may take a 
hit when these actual volumes flow through.

I realize that Kim is out and that you guys are stretched thin, however, a 
problem of this magnitude needs to be addressed as soon as it's discovered.  
Someone needs to be overriding the 0 volumes so that Sitara is receiving 
correct information and the P&L is kept as accurate as possible.

Please give me a call if you have any questions.

4	To: eric.bass@enron.com, o'neal.winfree@enron.com, julie.meyers@enron.com, 
5		kathryn.cordes@enron.com, jennifer.denny@enron.com,

7		michael.eiben@enron.com, karen.lambert@enron.com
8	Subject: FYI -New Product on EOL
9	Cc: brenda.herod@enron.com, sheri.thomas@enron.com, thomas.martin@enron.com, 
10		lisa.csikos@enron.com, steve.venturatos@enron.com,

12	Mime-Version: 1.0

14	Content-Transfer-Encoding: 7bit
15	Bcc: brenda.herod@enron.com, sheri.thomas@enron.com, thomas.martin@enron.com, 
16		lisa.csikos@enron.com, steve.venturatos@enron.com, 
17		connie.sutton@enron.com
18	X-From: Scott Mills
19	X-To: Eric Bass, O'Neal D Winfree, Julie Meyers, Kathryn Cordes, Jennifer deBoisblanc Denny, Dale Neuner, Daren J Farmer, Pat Clynes, Michael Eiben, Karen Lambert
20	X-cc: Brenda Herod, Sheri Thomas, Thomas A Martin, Lisa Csikos, Steve Venturatos, Connie Sutton
21	X-bcc: 
22	X-Folder: \Darren_Farmer_Dec2000\Notes Folders\Logistics
23	X-Origin: Farmer-D
24	X-FileName: dfarmer.nsf
25	
26	Just so everyone is on the same page:
27	
28	Based on Jennifer and Dale's discussions with Eric Bass, a new "tokenized 
29	period" will be set up in EOL.  The intent of this period (quick overview) is 
30	to allow for gas flow Monday through Friday and no flow on the weekends.  
31	This will generally be traded for in full month or rest of the month 
32	increments.
33	
34	It is my understanding the although the trade can be conveyed correctly to 
35	the customer and priced accordingly using EOL, the trade itself (with 
36	Multiple Monday - Friday, no flow during weekend periods) cannot be handled 
37	internally by EOL.  Just as EOL is not able to handle this trade, the Sitara 
38	bridge from EOL cannot handle this trade.  Because of this, there should be 
39	heighten attention by Trade Capture given to the EOL Bridge monitor.  These 
40	trades will error out and will have to be entered manually.
41	
42	An effort needs to be evaluated and prioritized by both applications (EOL and 
43	Sitara) on how a deal with multi-periods can flow without human 
44	intervention.  This has not been started.  In the meantime, a deal of this 
45	nature will have to be entered manually.
46

	dale.neuner@enron.com, daren.farmer@enron.com, pat.clynes@enron.com, 
	michael.eiben@enron.com, karen.lambert@enron.com
Subject: FYI -New Product on EOL
Cc: brenda.herod@enron.com, sheri.thomas@enron.com, thomas.martin@enron.com, 
	lisa.csikos@enron.com, steve.venturatos@enron.com, 
	connie.sutton@enron.com
Mime-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=us-ascii
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 7bit
Bcc: brenda.herod@enron.com, sheri.thomas@enron.com, thomas.martin@enron.com, 
	lisa.csikos@enron.com, steve.venturatos@enron.com, 
	connie.sutton@enron.com
X-From: Scott Mills
X-To: Eric Bass, O'Neal D Winfree, Julie Meyers, Kathryn Cordes, Jennifer deBoisblanc Denny, Dale Neuner, Daren J Farmer, Pat Clynes, Michael Eiben, Karen Lambert
X-cc: Brenda Herod, Sheri Thomas, Thomas A Martin, Lisa Csikos, Steve Venturatos, Connie Sutton
X-bcc: 
X-Folder: \Darren_Farmer_Dec2000\Notes Folders\Logistics
X-Origin: Farmer-D
X-FileName: dfarmer.nsf

Just so everyone is on the same page:

Based on Jennifer and Dale's discussions with Eric Bass, a new "tokenized 
period" will be set up in EOL.  The intent of this period (quick overview) is 
to allow for gas flow Monday through Friday and no flow on the weekends.  
This will generally be traded for in full month or rest of the month 
increments.

It is my understanding the although the trade can be conveyed correctly to 
the customer and priced accordingly using EOL, the trade itself (with 
Multiple Monday - Friday, no flow during weekend periods) cannot be handled 
internally by EOL.  Just as EOL is not able to handle this trade, the Sitara 
bridge from EOL cannot handle this trade.  Because of this, there should be 
heighten attention by Trade Capture given to the EOL Bridge monitor.  These 
trades will error out and will have to be entered manually.

An effort needs to be evaluated and prioritized by both applications (EOL and 
Sitara) on how a deal with multi-periods can flow without human 
intervention.  This has not been started.  In the meantime, a deal of this 
nature will have to be entered manually.

How do I know that a particular deal has multi-period flow?  Once the EOL 
product has been set up, Jennifer and/or Dale will let all involved know.  
The person(s) responsible for entering the deal will have to understand what 
is meant by the EOL product's delivery period and enter the deal 
accordingly.  

For example, assume that a deal has been traded for April:

  Four delivery periods (separate lines) should be included in the Sitara 
ticket
  
  Start: 04/03 Stop: 04/07
   04/10  04/14
   04/17  04/21
   04/24  04/28 
  
 Each delivery period (line) should have the same pricing

 Remember to enter the EOL deal number when creating the Sitara trade.

 Also remember that paths created in Unify assume the stop date is open 
ended.  Every effort needs to be made to make sure the appropriate end date 
is on the path; otherwise
 the number of reconciling items will increase.

Please forward this information to anyone else you think might be impacted.

Any concerns, please contact Sheri Thomas or myself.

SRM (x33548)

content.content: 54	- Hourly phone check-out of service-customer generators to BPA: Replace the hourly calls to Frontier and GCPUD and to BPA with an automatic meter-data feed to BPA and exception alerts to the RT desk.. Why: The mail already says these generators are to be metered automatically, by BPA, from mid-August 2001, and that the hourly calls stop then; so the proposal adds nothing, it treats a short episode as 730 hours a month for good, and its 3-minute figure is a split of a ceiling, not an estimate. Research that could settle it: Look for mail after August 2001 showing the hourly calls to BPA still being made for Frontier or another generator after automatic metering was due, and for what the call actually took each hour; without that the idea is not new and not ongoing.

 -----Original Message-----
From: 	Williams III, Bill  
Sent:	Wednesday, August 01, 2001 12:47 PM
To:	Anderson, John; Bland, Todd; Dean, Craig; Guzman, Mark; Harasin, Leaf; Linder, Eric; Merriss, Steven; Meyers, Bert; Porter, David V.; Slinger, Ryan; Solberg, Geir; Symes, Kate; Williams III, Bill
Subject:	Fastest Way to Handle Colstrip Cuts



When Colstrip goes down we will be short at Montana system and long at PGE System.  We need to buy a transmission wheel from BPA (Account#736780) from PGE System to the Montana System Border.  If need be we can also do a Buy-Resale with WWP to move the energy from PGE Sys/Mid-C/LOLO to the Montana System Border.  The method for documentation and cleaning up enpower are below.


1.)  Be sure to begin with a physical cut sheet (in drawer above SAR's).

2.) In enpower, build an index forward buy from PGE under STNW book for the total amount of mws cut due to colstrip going down.  Use the DOW JONES MIDC index (remember to specify in the index if it is on or off-peak).  Enter an offset of .10  .  

2.) Enter a transmission deal from BPA.   (MIDC to MPC SYS)  The transmission fee is $2.52.  Build the transmission deal under STNW.

3.) Go into deal scheduling and query  under the counterparty PGE.  Select all

4.) Bring up all deals of the counterparties involved at Colstrip---- specifically, Ashgrove,Conocpil, Energywesr, Louisiana Pacific, and Smurfit Stone, etc.
	(these enpower deal numbers can be located under the counterparties name in lotus notes.)

5.)Zero out the buy from PGE @MPC SYS

6.) Finally link the deals.

7.) Check real time postion manager, make sure you are flat.

8.) Make cuts in Lotus Notes Cuts Database (this is the most time consuming portion of this procedure).

9.) Make notes in Discussion Forum

10.) Email appropriate groups, Kate Symes, and myself.

If you have questions regarding this procedure please let me know.
Thanks,
Bill

3.) Try to have the counterparties continue any paths around us. Just "bow out" gracefully if you have no other options with the words "L - D's."

4.) If we are cut by a generator/utility going into California, we must call the HA desk at California and tell them the increment that we will be underscheduling our load by. For example, EPE will be cutting all schedules going into California on light load (100 mws). If we cannot resupply the schedules we need to tell the state that we are underscheduling our load by 100 mws. THIS IS EXTREMELY IMPORTANT. We have posted an LC with Cali for this reason.

Also, EPE will be long RT 100 mws off-peak as they are no longer selling to us. 25 mws should be sold to TEP to cover a forward schedule. Stacy has set this up at PV. Please do this as a direct bill with EPE. As of Jan 01, 2002 we will no longer be marketing for EPE. Also, PV#3 will be coming off this weekend, and FC#4 will be down from HE 22 on Saturday through HE 06 on Sunday.

This will probably not be a fun weekend. 
I appreciate your help. 

Bill

 -----Original Message-----

Sent:	Tuesday, August 14, 2001 11:13 AM
To:	Williams III, Bill
Subject:	A few reminders....

Bill - does this sound reasonable? Do you have anything to add?


Please make a note of the following. I know we have several new traders, and details often get overlooked in the midst of the learning process. But this is not only information for the new guys a reminder for the old that attention to detail is an important part of the job. Thanks.

1. Purchases made under one book must be sold under the same book. Pay attention when extending deals. If you don't purchase the energy in a particular book, you don't have energy to sell from that book.

2. Specify EPEC as the group when entering deals for El Paso. Also, pay attention to detail with EPE spinning reserves (as a violation is extremely expensive for EPE), also curtail units in the right order. Copper then Newman 4 then Four Corners (Be sure to curtail Four Corners before selling under cost!)

3. El Paso model must tie out with CARP when trading day is done. Check spreadsheet formulas. 

4. El Paso totals should be logged in the reconciliation model (m://electric/epe/epe01/aug01/epe reconciliation model) and all variances explained.

5. Bloomberg deals need to be assigned a $15 FLAT broker fee per trade. If you begin a deal with Bloomberg trades, enter a per-megawatt fee, and extend the deal later with bilateral trades, you're effectively charging yourself extra brokerage because THAT FEE WILL BE ASSIGNED TO EVERY MW IN YOUR DEAL. Can someone come up with a compelling reason why we wouldn't simply multiply $15 times the number of Bloomberg trades done? huh?Please let me know.

6. Most importantly, if you are unsure, call someone who is not.

Thanks again for your attention to these matters.

Kate

80	- Collecting biweekly time reports by email (Transwestern commercial group): Have each person record their own time off in the timekeeping system when it happens, so the assistant only reviews a list of exceptions instead of collecting email replies.. Why: The same work and the same change are already saved in decisions.md as "Pay-period time reports for the Transwestern commercial group", which cites the same Lokay time-report messages.
81	- Monthly accounting arrangement for meter 98-7266 (TGLO storage fuel at Bammel): Replace the hand-built monthly accounting arrangement for meter 7266 with a standing evergreen deal pair on contracts 012-41500-05-002 and 012-88494-05-001.. Why: The mail shows only two moments 20 months apart, does not show the monthly hand-build still happening in 2001 (Farmer was asked for a deal in Feb 2000), and by May 2001 the contracts were 'canceled or expired', so the October 2001 entry looks like cleanup after the storage flow ended, not ongoing monthly work. Research that could settle it: Look for mail after February 2000 showing whether Farmer set up the requested deal for 7266, and for any 7266 or TGLO Bammel storage volumes in months after May 2001; if neither exists, the work has ended and the idea fails.
82	- Waiting on Path Confirmation saves during nightly checkouts: Make Path Confirmation save confirmations in the background (or in one commit per counterparty) so the shift trader does not wait about a minute per save.. Why: The same work, the nightly Path Confirmation checkouts with the same background-save fix and the same messages (williams-w3/sent_items/86.eml and 62.eml), is already saved as item 2 in decisions.md.
83	- Wellhead spot/interim ticket requests to logistics: Producer Services enters wellhead spot and interim tickets in Sitara directly instead of emailing the terms to Texas logistics to type in.. Why: The mail shows about 9 requests in 7 months (about 1.3 a month, not 3) and only one bid-week list, not one a month. One cited 'resend' is really a new deal. It is also not shown that Producer Services can or may enter spot tickets: when asked to enter one directly, they passed it to logistics instead. Research that could settle it: Look for mail showing Producer Services entering spot or interim tickets in Sitara themselves, or a rule that keeps deal entry away from the people who negotiate the deal. Also look for more bid-week spot lists or ticket requests in other mailboxes that would raise the real count.
84	- Nightly real-time schedule checkout calls: Auto-match Enpower prescheduled paths against OATI e-tags so traders call only counterparties whose paths do not match. Why: The mail shows the tag record Enron sees is incomplete and that the nightly calls are what catch the problems, so matching against tags cannot safely replace the calls, and the claim that two thirds of calls would go away has no support. Research that could settle it: Mail showing that, over a normal stretch of weeks, Enron's tag data matched what counterparties actually scheduled, and how many paths and calls a typical night's checkout involved, could support a narrower version that only skips the manual save step for paths that match.
85	- Re-extending the TECO / El Paso Seven Oaks buy/sell tickets at meter 6884: Paper the Seven Oaks tailgate adjustment and book one evergreen purchase and one evergreen sale ticket at meter 6884, instead of extending or re-creating the tickets by email whenever settlements finds them expired.. Why: The work is a case of item 10 already saved in decisions.md ('Extending Sitara deals for meter flow outside the deal term'), which already cites 2095.eml from this thread, so saving it would count the same savings twice. The evidence also has errors: 983.eml's quotes are from April 1999 setup mail, not a March 2000 lapse; 2093/2095 and 2099 are one episode on 23 Feb 2001, not two; the proposal leaves out that George Weissman, who would have to paper it, said he was 'reluctant to open this can of worms' (1626.eml); and the counterparty-merge fix has nothing in the mail behind it. Research that could settle it: Show what the saved meter-flow exception list would not catch here, for example that 6884's buy/sell pair needs a new ticket rather than an extension. Count the real episodes: Jun 2000 (1626), 23 Feb 2001 (2093/2095/2099, replaced by El Paso deal 637225 in 2103), Apr 2001 (194/195/2149/2150), and Jul 2001 (95.eml, where 637225 had lapsed again). Find out whether the desk could book long-term tickets without the paper Weissman declined to draw up.

- Business continuity and contingency surveys, BCP seat testing, and weekend systems availability notices: Desk managers have to ask each scheduler to fill in a spreadsheet survey, and Pinion merges the replies into a master sheet by hand. - Regulatory filing burden: FERC requiring a tariff filing within one day of every change to a negotiated indexed rate: Mary Kay Miller calls it an 'administrative nightmare': a filing every time the rate changes, possibly daily. She suggests posting the rate on a website instead. Files: corpus/lokay-m/inbox/9.eml
- Corrections to counterparty and entity names in deal booking: Deals booked under wrong or invalid counterparty names (TXU Gas Distribution, Enbridge Consumers Gas, IDACORP) have to be re-booked by hand, suggesting reference data isn't controlled. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/40.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/209.eml
- Switching email addresses to the standard format across systems and business cards: Every employee has to update applications, business cards and outside contacts by the cutoff date. Files: corpus/giron-d/inbox/246.eml, corpus/giron-d/inbox/249.eml
- Monthly 'New Generation in WSCC' report: distribution changed from email to printed hard copies, and recipients must send their name, location and assistant to ask for a copy. Recipients also report errors back by hand.: A recurring monthly report sent to about 90 people now needs manual requests and printing. Kate Symes forwarded it to Bill Williams, who already gets it, so distribution is duplicated. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/108.eml
- Prior-period gas imbalance paybacks (Lobo payout) that the POPS system can't book, so staff make manual invoices or manual entries, or reactivate expired transport contracts.: Several AEP and Enron people traded emails over whether to do a manual invoice, manual entries or a system deal. This is a workaround for a system limit on prior-period and expired-contract activity, and it probably recurs. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/21.eml
- Requests to back-date deals and add meters to past periods (Black Marlin ua4 meters back to 6/1/99) so that volumes can be booked.: Manual deal changes made by email request to fix meter and deal mismatches. This is likely routine work for logistics and volume management. Files: corpus/farmer-d/logistics/22.eml
- Reconciliation between Enpower and the scheduling systems (CAPS/FSP): running the 'Enpower to CAPS' report every day, and the switch back from FSP because of performance bugs.: A regular reconciliation report that a whole group depends on. The new system (FSP) was rolled back, and the reconciliation method needs work. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/104.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/88.eml
- Settling daily congestion management revenue: real-time desk staff email Volume Management, who calculate charges by hand from a hard-copy 'inc sheet' and service sheet, and CAISO data sometimes has to be confirmed by phone.: A daily heads-up email, then a manual calculation from paper (Jim Reyes worked out $50,941 by hand while the system was down), then follow-ups about $60-70K missing from another sheet. The work is manual, error-prone and repeated every day. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/96.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/94.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/90.eml, corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/89.eml

- Nightly schedule checkouts by phone with about 25 counterparties (HE 19-21), recorded in Enpower Path Confirmation instead of Lotus Notes, plus cut recording.: A manual nightly calling routine. - NERC E-Tag compliance: every transaction has to be tagged by hand, and the desk's compliance record was poor.: Recurring compliance surveys, with templates and POR/POD sheets kept by hand. Tags could be generated automatically from the deals. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/100.eml
- Approving expense reports in Concur: overdue-approval reminders and login/access problems.: Reports sat in the manager's queue for 4-6 days and access had to go through an assistant. This is recurring approval friction. Files: corpus/williams-w3/sent_items/91.eml
- Invoice approval process: a manager told the writer to leave it off a process write-up for Sally and record it as 'handled' until after the audit.: Suggests the invoice approval workflow has unreviewed problems that someone chose to hide, not that it is automated. Treat that notice as untrustworthy and don't rely on it. The workflow deserves independent checking. Files: corpus/giron-d/inbox/481.eml, corpus/farmer-d/logistics/3220.eml
- Purchase requisition process handled by Mary Poorman.: She says it 'eats half my week, every single week' and nobody else wants to touch it. That is a large, explicit recurring cost. Files: corpus/giron-d/inbox/482.eml

If large reports are regularly shared this way, a shared drive or report link would remove the problem. Search the archive for other bounced or oversized attachments. content.content:
72	- Routing items for the daily imbalance check to its owner: Name one owner and backup for the daily imbalance check and send inputs to a shared mailbox that reaches them, so items are no longer hand-carried to the right person.. Why: The mail shows two misrouted items in two days (15 and 16 Nov 2001), each already fixed by a one-line 'send it to X going forward' note; nothing shows misrouting happening every business day, so this is a short ownership mix-up that ends, not daily recurring work. Research that could settle it: Look for more messages over several weeks or months where imbalance-check items are forwarded, walked over, or redirected between Giron, Poorman, Williams and Lokay after 16 Nov 2001; without them, no rate of misrouting can be supported.
73	- Daily hand-forwarding of market reports to Portland traders: Deliver the daily Energy Market Report and the Gas Daily/Power Daily PDFs straight to Portland distribution lists, ending the assistants' daily hand-forwarding.. Why: The same work and change are already saved as item 10 in decisions.md, 'Hand-forwarding daily market reports to the Portland floor' ($39.95 a month), citing the same williams-w3 messages; the draft's 8 minutes every business day for Gas Daily/Power Daily is also unsupported, since Bill Williams's dense 1/28-2/6 inbox holds all 7 Energy Market Report forwards but only one Gas Daily/Power Daily send (1/31) and one 'not loaded yet' note (2/4).
74	- Monthly Investor Relations volume-variance explanations: Pre-draft each region's volume-variance explanation from a system breakdown (EnronOnline vs. other deals, top counterparty changes) so desk contacts only confirm or edit it.. Research that could settle it: Look for more messages over several weeks or months where imbalance-check items are forwarded, walked over, or redirected between Giron, Poorman, Williams and Lokay after 16 Nov 2001; without them, no rate of misrouting can be supported.

content.text: The purchase-requisition idea was already rejected for thin evidence, and 3221 looks like synthetic data from a single message, so I'm passing on both. Next is the FERC tariff-filing lead.

I feel we need to discuss with Columbia, INGAA and join in filing for rehearing on this administrative nightmare.  An alternative would be to require you to post on Internet website the day of the transaction the actual rate, so similarly situated customers would have access to the actual rate.  I'm sending you guys a copy of the order.
